name: Tierra Azul
headline: Community Resources & Housing Development Corp. (CRHDC) is building 46 new rental apartments for individuals and families at 30% to 80% AMI at 800 Craft Drive in Alamosa, the first rental phase of its 43-acre Tierra Azul neighborhood, and won 2025 Round One federal 9% and state credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It shows how a rural 9% deal got over the line once the city and nonprofit paid for the infrastructure separately with state and philanthropic grants (about $6M) and the city waived over $1M in fees; earlier tries in 2023 failed on infrastructure cost and readiness.

status.label: Under construction (per architect, May 2026)
status.detail: Infrastructure work began after a 2025-03-24 groundbreaking. In April 2026 the Alamosa News reported water, sewer, streets and sidewalks in place and foundations being poured in phase one, and on 2026-05-20 the architect KEPHART said the 46-unit phase is actively under construction with completion expected in May 2027. No CHFA closing record or certificate of occupancy was found.

next_step: Watch for certificates of occupancy and lease-up of the 46 apartments around May 2027 (the city says infrastructure completion is a condition of occupancy).

key_numbers.meaning: 26 one-bedroom, 16 two-bedroom and 4 three-bedroom units across one 30-unit building and two 8-plexes, serving 30% to 80% AMI with income averaging.
About $16M over the 10-year credit period, plus $650,000 in state credit.
Approved by the State Housing Board for the 46 apartments, announced 2025-12-31.
City of Alamosa contribution, per the application; separate grants of about $6.1M from DOLA paid for infrastructure for the first 137 units of the neighborhood.

background.text: City staff first met CRHDC about the site in January 2020. CRHDC bought the parcel in 2021, it was annexed into the city in June 2022, and the PUD/Preliminary Development Plan application was complete on 2023-02-16.

The PDP divides the site into three planning areas and asks for the designation to run for 25 years. The PUD letter describes six phases over 25 years. Final Development Plans are decided by the Planning Commission and ratified by City Council.

CRHDC first sought 9% credits in 2023 Round One with partners Overland Property Group and The Espinosa Group: 44 units in the December 2022 letter of intent and 46 units, all at or below 60% AMI, in the application. It was not awarded (inferred from the later resubmission); the 2025 application says infrastructure funding had been the obstacle to readiness.

For 2025 the infrastructure was fully funded and contracted for the 2025 construction season. City staff confirmed infrastructure completion is needed for certificates of occupancy but not building permits; site plan approval was in hand and the city offered a 30-day building permit review.

City planning minutes in January and March 2025 said infrastructure would start in March 2025, self-help single-family homes would follow that summer, and build-out of the first two phases would take about four years. The developer obtained a CDOT access permit for the whole development.
The city held a groundbreaking at 800 South Craft Drive on 2025-03-24 for the infrastructure phase.
CRHDC's offices are about a quarter mile away; it plans on-site services such as ESL classes, financial literacy, health education and housing stability counseling.

discrepancies.text: The full neighborhood is described as 412 units by the PUD letter and KEPHART, 406 units by Construction Reporter, 396 units by the 2023 application, and a maximum of 440 units in the city staff report.
KEPHART calls the 46 apartments Phase 1, while local reports describe phase one as 137 residential units.
The PUD letter and Construction Reporter say build-out will take about 25 years, while the Alamosa News says the phases will be completed over about the next ten years.
City records say CRHDC bought the land in 2021, while Enterprise says the CRHDC team secured land in 2020.
